newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl- enthusiasm doesn't mean easing EMU criteria.
newsitem.headline: Kohl- enthusiasm doesn't mean easing EMU criteria.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl cautioned on Friday his enthusiasm for European integration did not mean he would tolerate any weakening of the Maastricht criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU).

"I warn against misunderstanding my commitment to Europe along the lines of 'Kohl is so enthusiastic about Europe that he'll go soft on the stability crieria at the end'," Kohl told the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung newspaper.

Kohl told Saturday's edition of the newspaper in an interview, released to news organisations ahead of publication, that he would guard the tradition of stability, which has been the hallmark of the deutschemark.

"Anyone who is ready to introduce the euro in place of the mark, as I am, knows that the Germans' experience with the mark is one of the best in history and that we will not give up this accomplishment in the future," the chancellor said.
He also said he was against politicians in one country giving opinions on the chances of another meeting the EMU criteria.
"I am in favour of everyone -- including Germany -- doing their own homework. There's a lot to do. And I'm in favour of the criteria in the (Maastricht) treaty being applied strictly."
